First retrospective (runs 1-10). Headline: the loop generates good adjustments but has no channel to apply them - only 4 of 11 critique-proposed adjustments across 23 days ever reached LOOP.md or the scripts, and the branch-tips cache took 5 flaggings over 3 weeks to land. The graduation gate is technically met (0 false_positives, 0 escalations across 10 runs) but must NOT be read as evidence: false_positives is fed exclusively by a human [FP] mark that has never once been made, so 0 is an absence of measurement, not precision - the same silent-zero class as a mis-scoped test glob. Two thresholds have never fired and structurally cannot (cache hit rate <50% against an observed 0.96-0.99 band; 2x-trailing-median output tokens against a 17k-1.98M range). Local repo hygiene was the noisiest source in 7 of 10 runs, and its ~/projects/* scan root does not exist on work-it at all. duration_s was recorded as 0 on runs 9-10 and is estimated here. 8 numbered refinements proposed to the human; none applied pending approval.

Application record for the 2026-08-06 retrospective (the prior line is the analysis). Refinements 1-6 approved and applied to LOOP.md via the loop-design skill; 7-8 held; L2 promotion held by user decision despite the gate being literally met. Applying refinement 6 exposed a contradiction in the L1 boundary statement - the header said the loop never commits or pushes, while the loop has always had to commit its own STATE.md/runs.jsonl - so the boundary was rewritten to scope read-only strictly to the TRIAGED repos and to name the loop-state write as the single deliberate exception. Level unchanged at 1, so no promotion event. Next retrospective should verify these six actually stayed in LOOP.md: only 4 of the 11 adjustments proposed across runs 1-10 ever landed, and nothing in the protocol notices when one does not.

critique: Applied branch-staleness-by-commits-ahead, previously HELD the same day and then approved by explicit decision. Deviated from the literal proposal on purpose and said so in the ledger row: run 5 asked to replace tip-date staleness WITH commits-ahead, but commits-ahead measures divergence, not time - a branch 3 ahead and untouched 60 days would have scored identically to one created this morning. The real defect was narrower: git rebase preserves the author date and writes a new committer date, and the protocol never specified which one it read. So staleness now pins to the tip AUTHOR date, and ahead_by is recorded as a SEPARATE signal (0-ahead + stale = dead weight to delete; 12-ahead + stale = unmerged work at risk). Adding ahead_by threatened to reintroduce the per-branch API call whose removal took five proposals over three weeks, so the branch_tips cache was extended rather than bypassed: author_date refetches only on a branch SHA change, ahead_by also on a DEFAULT-branch SHA change since it is relative to a moving base, and pre-today cache entries with a bare date field are treated as a miss because there is no way to know which date they held. Ledger now 10 of 11 landed, 1 held, 0 outstanding.

adjustment.text: Staleness on tip author date; ahead_by as a separate divergence signal

critique: Applied cache-quiet-repo-pr-issue-results, previously HELD the same day then approved by explicit decision - and again deviated from the proposal text on purpose. Run 9 asked to cache a no-PRs/no-issues answer for repos confirmed quiet twice running. That is not the same shape as the branch_tips cache it was modelled on: branch_tips skips expensive calls only AFTER one cheap authoritative call proves nothing changed, whereas caching a quiet-repo negative has no detector at all and creates a window where a newly opened PR goes unreported - a false negative on a loop whose only job is surfacing things. Verified against gh 2.95.0 that gh search prs --owner supports --json, then smoke-tested it live: one call returned both open fleet PRs (TokenMonitor #1 and #2), matching STATE.md exactly. So the per-repo sweep across ~17 repos was ELIMINATED in favour of two fleet-wide calls rather than cached - same cost saving, zero staleness. Added an explicit --limit and truncation check, since gh search defaults to 30 and a truncated list reads as fewer open PRs. Ledger now 11 of 11 landed, 0 held, 0 outstanding - every adjustment proposed across runs 1-10 is applied.

adjustment.text: Fleet-wide gh search for PRs/issues instead of a per-repo sweep

critique: First run under the post-retrospective protocol; every one of the seven refinements exercised. Biggest win was ahead_by: NMMTools codex/remote-business-tools and feature/wpf-gui are 0 ahead / 59 behind, so five runs of "18 days stale, tracking only" became "carries no work, delete it" - age alone could never have said that. Repo discovery found 12 local repos where ~/projects/* had been silently returning empty, so every prior runs local-hygiene result on work-it was unverified rather than clean. The revised spend threshold fired correctly on its first run (808,943 output tokens, past both the 750k floor and 2x the 177,083 median) on a genuinely heavy session. false_positives is 0 for a stated reason, not by silence: refinement 1 needs three consecutive runs of byte-identical history before it can fire, and this is run 1. One real miss found in the old state: a Resolved entry claiming no mwgrant21/claude-config repo exists is now false - the repo exists and the local clone tracks it - and that entry had told future runs to SKIP the repo, so a stale resolution was actively suppressing a check. Adjustment for next run: exclude DEFAULT branches from the >14-day staleness rule. It flagged Jira-Autoticketing/master (29d), learning-profile/main (24d) and cli-shared-memory/master (15d), which are dormant repos rather than stale feature work - three of six staleness hits were this shape.

critique: Applied exclude-default-branches-from-staleness, proposed by this same days run-11 critique - the first adjustment to go from proposal to applied inside a single run, against a prior average measured in weeks. Implemented LITERALLY this time, unlike refinements 7 and 8: the literal reading has no hole here, because a default branch age is not a staleness signal and the two things that DO matter are already covered elsewhere (unmerged work by ahead_by, unpushed local work by local hygiene). Default branch author dates are still recorded in notes.branch_tips - excluded from the FINDING, not from the data. Ledger now 12 of 12 landed.

critique: Run 12. The revised CACHE threshold fired for the first time (91.3% vs a 0.978 five-run median, 6.5pp below the 5pp trigger) and it is a low-volume artifact: today's entire sample is 39 input / 6,831 output tokens, essentially this triage run alone, so a handful of requests move the ratio. The threshold is not wrong - it fired at its first real opportunity, which the pre-retrospective 50% bar never could - it just has no denominator gate. That is the adjustment: gate-cache-flag-on-min-volume. The SPEND half of the same refinement behaved perfectly by contrast, firing on yesterday's 808,943 and going silent today at 6,831 with no edit. Noisiest source was GitHub branch staleness again, but for a better reason than before: after exclude-default-branches-from-staleness, every remaining staleness hit is a genuine non-default branch, and 2 of the 4 (the NMMTools 0-ahead pair) are the SAME recommendation for a second run running - they are the first items in line to auto-count as loop-derived noise on run 13 under refinement 1. The branch-tips cache served 19 of 23 branches. Two 'new' local repos (TriageDesk, uw-mail-router) turned out to be clones of Jira-Autoticketing and RoundRobin - discovery finds clones, not repos, and the digest must say which remote a local clone points at or it invents fleet growth that is not there.

critique: Run 13. Cleanest fleet state the loop has seen: ZERO open PRs and ZERO open issues (down from 3 PRs), and all four stale remote branches are now 0 ahead, so every staleness finding this run is losslessly deletable dead weight. The empty gh search prs result was NOT taken at face value - it was re-verified with a per-repo gh pr list drill-down, because 'no open PRs' and 'the search source is broken' render identically in a digest and this loop's only job is surfacing things. The revised CACHE threshold cleared on its own (95.7% vs a 0.978 median, 2.1pp, inside the 5pp trigger) with no edit, and today was ANOTHER low-volume day (15,603 output tokens) - so the outstanding gate-cache-flag-on-min-volume adjustment now has one low-volume day that fired and one that did not, which weakens rather than strengthens run 12's case for it. Refinement 5 fired for the first time ever: claude-token-tracker held 1 dirty line (?? .claude/) unchanged across 3 runs. false_positives is NON-ZERO for the first time (1, loop-derived: the NMMTools 0-ahead pair, same recommendation ignored for 3 runs), which finally feeds the counter the L2 graduation gate reads. But feeding it exposed a mechanical defect, and that is this run's adjustment: noise-match-on-finding-identity-not-text. Refinement 1's literal test is 'byte-identical across 3 consecutive runs', yet every GitHub staleness item embeds an age in days that increments every run (20d -> 23d here), so no such item can EVER be byte-identical and the counter can never fire on its own terms - I counted the pair on the rule's INTENT, not its letter. That is the same un-fireable-check class the 2026-08-06 retrospective just removed from the spend and cache thresholds, reintroduced one refinement later. Fix: key loop-derived noise on a stable finding identity (repo + branch + recommendation), not on rendered text. Noisiest source was GitHub branch staleness again (4 of 16 findings), for the third run running. One process note: the batched local-hygiene sweep MISREPORTED Aether-OS-livetest as 1 dirty line when git status --porcelain actually returns 3; a direct re-run of the count is what caught it, and refinement 5's stale-WIP rule reads that exact number - a wrong count there silently flips a flag. Verify counts the flag depends on directly, never from inside a batched loop whose output was not spot-checked.
